snippet.title: What Will NASA's Roman Telescope Reveal on Dec 7?
snippet.description:
On Monday, December 7, 2026 at 20:30 UTC (3:30 p.m. EST), NASA will unveil the very first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope live from the AGU Annual Meeting on nasa.gov/live.

Launched on August 30, 2026 to a million-mile orbit at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2, Roman uses a 2.4-metre primary mirror — the exact same size as Hubble's — yet its 288-megapixel Wide Field Instrument captures a patch of sky bigger than a full Moon in a single snapshot, at least 100 times larger than Hubble's field of view. From L2, it will hunt dark energy, dark matter, and worlds beyond our solar system. You can watch the unveiling live on December 7 and even claim your own cosmic pixel through NASA's Adopt a Pixel campaign (science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/adopt-a-pixel/).

Watch our deep-space telescope film next: JWST Found Galaxies That Shouldn't Exist Yet (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ziKBPJ6FY0U)

Sources: NASA Headquarters Media Advisory M26-088, 'NASA Invites Media, Public to View Roman Telescope's First Images' (17 Nov 2026, nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-invites-media-public-to-view-roman-telescopes-first-images/); NASA Science, 'Wide Field Instrument — Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope' (science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/wide-field-instrument/); NASA Science, 'Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Overview' (science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/); NASA Science, 'Roman Frequently Asked Questions' (science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/frequently-asked-questions/); NASA Science, 'Adopt a Pixel' (science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/adopt-a-pixel/).

Image credits: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center / Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS #15081 'Roman Mission Trailer', Ernie Wright SVS #5587 unlabelled plain Moon); NASA / Kennedy Space Center (KSC-20260830 Falcon Heavy launch footage); NASA / ESA / STScI (Hubble Ultra Deep Field GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001061, Hubble eXtreme Deep Field GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001651). Pictures: NASA/ESA imagery alongside our own scale graphics. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
